summary: Fri 01 Aug 2026. Wrote DA3-Streaming integration spec (docs/plans/plan-da3-streaming-20260801.md), researched against upstream source not the README. Four findings that change the approach: (1) da3_streaming/ is NOT pip-installed - pyproject declares packages=[src/depth_anything_3] and the streaming tree lives at repo root with its own requirements.txt/configs/fastloop/loop_utils, so it must be vendored via COPY. (2) It replaces the SfM stage, NOT --gs-only: outputs are camera_poses.txt (flattened 4x4 C2W) + intrinsic.txt + pcd/combined_pcd.ply + loop_closures.txt, so it feeds splatfacto and upgrades da3-standard while da3-draft stays the 76s preview. (3) Three keys in the user's proposed config (input_width, input_height, precision) DO NOT EXIST in base_config.yaml - resolution is set by pre-resizing frames; real defaults are Model.chunk_size=120 / Model.overlap=60 nested under Model:, not 65/22 flat. (4) Proposed 65-chunk @ 672x378 will not fit 24GB: 60 @ 504x378 is already 21.2/24GB, and at patch-14 the proposal is 84,240 tokens vs 58,320 = 1.44x, so linear scaling alone lands ~30GB. Plan starts from benchmarked 60/30 @ 504x378 with upstream's 50pct overlap on a10g-small. Extra deps flagged: faiss-gpu (highest risk, PyPI version unmaintained; loop_enable:False is the phase-1 escape hatch), numba (JIT warmup), pypose. Weights are local file paths not HF IDs, and loop closure needs a separate DINO-SALAD checkpoint we do not fetch at all. Highest-risk piece identified: the pose converter, since streaming emits C2W where existing da3_to_transforms expects w2c and inverts - wrong convention trains cleanly while being wrong, so phase 2 validates trajectory against the known-good da3-standard run before spending on training.
